title: Discoveries & the biblical record
concept: An evidence desk: objects lead to bounded historical questions. Terracotta marks interpretations and supplements; patinated green marks connections and preserved wording. Shared typography, header and transitions retained.
sequence: Six object cases, each with three inspectable details and graded conclusions
Lachish: four sources compared across three questions
A destruction date reconsidered; a later architectural correction
Pilate, Mesha and Tel Dan: restoration, disputed marks and disputed joins
Cyrus and Ezra: compare authority, action/place and document
Six scholarly pathways, source register and explicit gaps
strongestInsights: Different sources are useful because they answer different questions, not because their number constitutes proof.
Changing a fragment arrangement can alter a reconstructed narrative without erasing a preserved dynastic name.
A contextual policy parallel is not a duplicate decree.
Later excavation can correct an architectural reconstruction without overturning a campaign date.
interactions: Eighteen close-reading annotations across six shareable object states
Three evidence disclosures and provenance per object
Sixteen combinations of four campaign sources, evaluated against three historical questions
Three paired Mesha disagreements with both arguments visible
Tel Dan textual relationship diagram with proposed link separated from preserved words
Three claim checks with feedback and restart
visualizations: Categorical evidence matrix; no probability scores
Original schematic ramp/counter-ramp section, no measured geometry or construction totals
Tel Dan textual relationship diagram, not a facsimile or proposed physical join
accessibility: Distinct React keys preserve exactly one close reading on selection
Responsive table confined to a labeled, keyboard-focusable horizontal scrolling region
All source links identify new-tab behavior
assets: Original SVG and textual diagrams only. Actual epigraphic images linked through source records; no reproduction rights assumed.
research: 33 source records with access limits; claim-level source IDs in durable dossier. Includes original excavation sections, critical-edition extracts and research through 2025. Does not claim exhaustive coverage or full reading of inaccessible works.
releaseSource: .local/release-atlas-loop; only this study’s five source files and two research/design files mirrored.
deployment: None. Existing preview at http://127.0.0.1:8931 only.
